[About]{.eyebrow}

## The short version

John Dellipriscoli is an economist and educator whose work bridges applied economics, finance, and the business of sport. He is an Assistant Professor of Business in the School of Business and Technology at Holy Family University, where he teaches across economics and accounting.

Before moving into academia full time, John spent roughly five years in applied economic work — producing economic, demographic, and financial forecasts, designing impact analyses, and serving as a forensic economic expert witness in civil litigation. That practitioner's grounding shapes his teaching: he keeps the focus on the real decisions behind the models.

John's research centers on the economics and organization of sport, which anchors both his Economics of Sport teaching and his doctoral work. He is currently completing an Ed.D. in Organizational Leadership at Holy Family University.
:::
:::

## What I teach

::: {.section-lead}
Undergraduate economics and accounting, across in-person and asynchronous online sections. My aim is to connect theory to the decisions students actually face — drawing on an applied forecasting and consulting background to keep the material concrete.
:::

### Holy Family University {.course-head}

::: {.courses}
- [ECON 203]{.code} Microeconomics
- [ECON 204]{.code} Macroeconomics
- [SPMM 310]{.code} Economics of Sport
- [PPES 381]{.code} Money, Banking & Financial Markets
- [ACCT 205]{.code} Financial Accounting
- [ACCT 206]{.code} Managerial Accounting
- [ACCT 416]{.code} Government & Non-Profit Accounting
:::

### Norwich University {.course-head}

::: {.courses}
- [EC201/202]{.code} Macro & Microeconomics
- [EC106]{.code} The World Economy
- [EC299]{.code} Sports Economics
- [EC310]{.code} Money & Banking
- [EC419]{.code} International Economics
- [CS120]{.code} Business Applications & Problem-Solving

## Research & scholarship

::: {.interests}
- Sports economics — leagues, labor markets, and player valuation
- International trade and economic development
- Applied microeconomics and financial forecasting
- Forensic and applied economic analysis
- Organizational leadership and performance
:::

::: {.wip}
[Work in progress]{.tag}

My doctoral research examines player development and organizational performance in professional soccer academies, connecting leadership climate to on-field and roster-value outcomes. *Ed.D. in Organizational Leadership, expected December 2028.*
:::
:::
